input.quote: 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.
input.rationale: § 8.2 matches the preferred position: renewals are single twelve-month periods (no multi-year auto-renewal), Customer may opt out on only thirty days' written notice, and Vendor must send a renewal reminder sixty days beforehand — with the opt-out deadline extended if the reminder is missed, which removes the residual Customer notice burden. § 8.3 caps renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and three percent, requires ninety days' notice of any increase, and excludes prepaid periods, satisfying the price-predictability and prepaid-protection elements. § 8.1's three-year master term is not a renewal term and continues only to govern outstanding Order Forms. No redline needed.
